What if I'm nervous about IRC because it has a reputation for being an environment where hackers can harm your computer and/or real life?

This is a pretty common thing I'm hearing lately. So let me address it bluntly: We will not tolerate that kind of conduct on our network, and we have safeguards in place to protect your identifiable information (IP address). When you connect to our servers, only a handful of IRCops (network admins) can see your actual IP address, but normal users see a "masked" version. Additionally, you can request a vHost (a mask) to completely get rid of the rest of the information. On a personal note, my profession is within Computer Security, and I regularly ensure things are to my standards (the IRCops can verify, I can be a little demanding at times).

IRC networks have been tarnished by a select few, but using a network such as Freenode as an example, has helped very large active communities be able to communicate extremely quick, and offers a level of support for their projects you just can't get through any other means.

As with any service, you should be careful what you click on, or what information you give out. There are bad people out there, but we strive to make our network safe for everyone as we can.
Thanks for taking the time to respond :-) My question was solely about reputation, not mechanics, and your answer is perfect.
Can vouch for security, we take that and privacy very seriously.
hey just curious whats the benefit of goat chat versus just posting on voat? Response time?

Is that the ONLY benefit to IRC over structured forums?

I don't think so. I think the instant response does something else beyond allowing you to discuss things faster. It makes a stronger sense of community. Instead of us talking ON a website and refreshing the page every few mins, we're talking IN IRC. That probably doesn't make a lot of sense unless you've hung around on an IRC channel for a while.

Also, the other main advantage is you get to choose who you're talking to, and who sees the information you want to share. On Voat, anybody can come and join in the discussion you're having, which isn't always a good thing.
